# 1. Read Data (SKIP IF YOU DO NOT NEED TO PULL FROM ORACLE)

Pull data from its source: Manual data: data/unformatted data. Automated data: Add script for data call (API, package, etc.). Confidential data: Store locally in the confidential data folder - This folder is excluded using gitignore and will not push to the GitHub repo. If intermediate data (shapefiles etc.) are needed, please put them in data\>intermediate - Filename should use the syntax rootname_descriptivename

Guidance for the rec data: https://sefsc.github.io/SEFSC-dolphin-analyses/MRIP.html

```{r}
Sys.setenv(TZ = "UTC", ORA_SDTZ = "UTC")

# Define your username
my_username <- "CGERVASI"

# Connect using stored keyring password
con <- dbConnect(dbDriver("Oracle"), 
                 username = my_username,
                 password = key_get("SECPR_Oracle", my_username),
                 dbname = "SECPR")
```

```{r}

```


save the dataset 
```{r}
head(ACL.raw)
str(ACL.raw)

#first we will subset to the Gulf. That is SUB_REG = 7. 

ACL.gulf = ACL.raw %>% 
  subset(SUB_REG == 7)

write_csv(ACL.gulf, here("data/intermediate/gulf_rec_landings_raw.csv"))
```


# 2. Clean data and create time series csv

Transform the data to fit the IEA data format.
For more info on IEA data format go to the IEAnalyzeR vignette [HERE](https://gulf-iea.github.io/IEAnalyzeR/articles/How_to_use_IEAnalyzeR.html).
Once data are formatted with time (annual or monthly) as column 1 and metric values in the remaining columns, you can use the function convert_cleaned_data to convert your csv into a format that can be read by the data_prep function. Replace "your_data" in the code below with whatever your dataframe is called.

```{r}
ACL.raw = read_csv(here("data/intermediate/gulf_rec_landings_raw.csv"))



#Now let's just get a list of all the species in the dataset and their total landings
gulf_specs = ACL.gulf %>% 
  group_by(NEW_COM) %>% 
  summarize(
    GOM_LABEL = first(GOM_LABEL),
    total_landings = sum(LBSEST_SECWWT, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% 
  arrange(GOM_LABEL, NEW_COM)

#save this to look at more closely
write_csv(gulf_specs, here("data/intermediate/gulf_rec_specs_list.csv"))
```

```{r}
clean_data <- ACL.gulf %>%
  filter(!is.na(YEAR))
```

clean the dataset to only keep species within Gulf Council Finfish FMPs, the Coastal Migratory Pelagics (CMP) FMP, and the red drum FMP. 
https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/federally-managed-gulf-america-reef-fish
https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/management-plan/gulf-and-south-atlantic-coastal-migratory-pelagic-fishery-management-plan 
https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/management-plan/gulf-red-drum-fishery-management-plan 
```{r}
# Strictly verified GMFMC-managed finfish species
gmfmc_finfish_official <- c(
  # Reef Fish FMP - Snappers
  "red snapper", "vermilion snapper", "gray snapper", "lane snapper", 
  "mutton snapper", "yellowtail snapper", "cubera snapper", "silk snapper", 
  "blackfin snapper", "queen snapper", "wenchman",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Groupers
  "gag", "red grouper", "scamp", "yellowedge grouper", 
  "black grouper", "yellowfin grouper", "yellowmouth grouper", 
  "snowy grouper", "warsaw grouper", "goliath grouper", "nassau grouper", "speckled hind",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Tilefishes
  "golden tilefish", "blueline tilefish", "goldface tilefish",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Jacks
  "greater amberjack", "lesser amberjack", "almaco jack", "banded rudderfish",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Others
  "gray triggerfish", "hogfish", 
  
  # Coastal Migratory Pelagics (CMP) FMP
  "king mackerel", "spanish mackerel", "cobia",
  
  # Red Drum FMP
  "red drum"
)

# Filter landings to strictly official GMFMC finfish

dat_managed <- clean_data %>%
  filter(NEW_COM %in% gmfmc_finfish_official,
         YEAR < 2026)

managed_finfish <- dat_managed %>% 
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
   mutate(
    land_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6,
  ) %>% 
  summarise(
    total_mil_lbs = sum(land_mil_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  select(YEAR, total_mil_lbs)

write_csv(dat_managed, here("data/intermediate/managed_species_landings_by_species_rec.csv"))
write_csv(managed_finfish, here("data/intermediate/gulf_managed_species_rec_landings_1981_present.csv"))
```

```{r}
# Cumulative Landings Pareto Analysis
pareto_df <- dat_unmanaged %>%
  group_by(NEW_COM) %>%
  mutate(
    land_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6,
  ) %>% 
  summarise(
    total_mil_lbs = sum(land_mil_lbs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_mil_lbs)) %>%
  mutate(
    RANK = row_number(),
    CUM_LBS = cumsum(total_mil_lbs),
    CUM_PCT = (CUM_LBS / sum(total_mil_lbs)) * 100
  )

write_csv(pareto_df, here("data/intermediate/unmanaged_rec_species_pareto_analysis.csv"))
```

Ok now we have a better handle on which marine/coastal finfish are the major commercially harvested unmanaged species. The top 33 species make up 90% of the landings. So let's just plot those. 

```{r}
# Top unmanaged recreational food/game fish species (~90% cumulative landings)
top_unmanaged_food_fish <- c(
  "spotted seatrout", "sheepshead", "black drum", "dolphin", 
  "striped mullet", "sand seatrout", "white grunt", "little tunny", 
  "southern flounder", "atlantic croaker", "hardhead catfish", "blackfin tuna", 
  "crevalle jack", "gafftopsail catfish", "bluefish", "southern kingfish", 
  "gulf kingfish", "yellowfin tuna", "blacktip shark", "great barracuda", 
  "ladyfish", "wahoo", "florida pompano", "black sea bass", 
  "gulf flounder", "common snook", "red porgy"
)

# Top unmanaged recreational bait/forage fish species
top_unmanaged_bait_forage <- c(
  "pinfish", "scaled sardine", "blue runner", 
  "gulf menhaden", "atlantic thread herring", "round scad"
)
```

Now we can get the unmanaged data!

```{r}

dat_unmanaged <- clean_data %>%
  filter(
    NEW_COM %in% c(top_unmanaged_food_fish, top_unmanaged_bait_forage),
    YEAR < 2026
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    land_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6,
    # Assign species category for conditional grouping
    Species_Type = case_when(
      NEW_COM %in% top_unmanaged_food_fish   ~ "Food",
      NEW_COM %in% top_unmanaged_bait_forage ~ "Bait"
    )
  )

# 2. Summarize annual totals into 4 distinct columns
unmanaged_summary <- dat_unmanaged %>% 
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
  summarise(
    food_mil_lbs     = sum(land_mil_lbs[Species_Type == "Food"], na.rm = TRUE),
    bait_mil_lbs     = sum(land_mil_lbs[Species_Type == "Bait"], na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% 
  select(YEAR, food_mil_lbs, bait_mil_lbs)

# Save intermediate summary CSVs
write_csv(dat_unmanaged, here("data/intermediate/rec_unmanaged_species_landings_by_species.csv"))
write_csv(unmanaged_summary, here("data/intermediate/rec_gulf_unmanaged_species_landings_1981_present.csv"))
```

Finally, clean total landings for all species

```{r}
dat_all <- clean_data %>%
  filter(
         YEAR < 2026)

dat_all <- dat_all %>% 
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
   mutate(
    land_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6,
  ) %>% 
  summarise(
    total_mil_lbs = sum(land_mil_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  select(YEAR, total_mil_lbs)

write_csv(dat_all, here("data/intermediate/gulf_all_species_rec_landings_1981_present.csv"))
```

# 3. Save Formatted data as csv

This will save your data to the appropriate folder.
```{r}
write.csv(formatted_assessed_finfish, file = csv_filename1, row.names = F)
write.csv(formatted_unmanaged_finfish, file = csv_filename2, row.names = F)
write.csv(formatted_all_finfish, file = csv_filename3, row.names = F)
```


# 4. Create Data_Prep object

Please use your formatted csv to create a "data_prep" object.
For more info on the data_prep function see the vignette linked above.
```{r}
data_obj1<-IEAnalyzeR::data_prep(csv_filename1)
data_obj2<-IEAnalyzeR::data_prep(csv_filename2, subind = "extent")
data_obj3<-IEAnalyzeR::data_prep(csv_filename3)
```

# 5. Save Formatted data_prep object

This will save your data to the appropriate folder.
```{r}
saveRDS(data_obj1, file = object_filename1)
saveRDS(data_obj2, file = object_filename2)
saveRDS(data_obj3, file = object_filename3)
```

# 6. Preview Plot

Use the IEAnalyzeR plotting function to preview the data.
This will not necessarily be the final figure used in reports.
For more info on the plot_fn_obj function go HERE

```{r}
IEAnalyzeR::plot_fn_obj(df_obj = data_obj1, trend = TRUE, sep_ylabs = TRUE, manual_title = "Recreational Landings of Managed Finfish", fig.width = 10)
ggsave(filename = plot_filename1, width = 10)

IEAnalyzeR::plot_fn_obj(df_obj = data_obj2, trend = TRUE, sep_ylabs = TRUE, manual_title = "Recreational Landings of Unmanaged Finfish", ylab_sublabel = c("extent", "unit"), fig.width = 10)
ggsave(filename = plot_filename2, width = 10)

IEAnalyzeR::plot_fn_obj(df_obj = data_obj3, trend = TRUE, sep_ylabs = TRUE, manual_title = "Recreational Landings of All Species", fig.width = 10)
ggsave(filename = plot_filename3, width = 10)
```
